title: CRLR/126/2018 of Manish Chandra Joshi Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
CRLR No.126 of 2018
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.

Mr. Manish Chandra Joshi, revisionist in person.
 Mr. P.S. Bohra AGA for the State of Uttarakhand.
 Mr. Jai Gopal, Advocate holding brief of Mr.
Vinay Kumar, Advocate for respondent no.2(iii).
 At the time when Criminal Revision was filed on
02.05.2018 respondent no.2(i) was serving as Assistant
Garrison Engineer (Electrical/Mechanical) Military
Services, Haldwani; and respondent no.2(ii) was
serving as Senior Engineer (Electrical/Mechanical)
Military Engineer Services, Haldwani. The revision was
listed as fresh on 16.05.2018, while admitting the
revision Court issued notices to all the respondents i.e.
2(i) to 2 (iii). Revisionist took notice and steps were
taken for serving respondents. The Registry on
24.05.2018, reported that respondents were unserved,
because respondent no.2(ii) was transferred as Chief
Engineer, Jodhpur, Rajasthan. This Court on
19.07.2018, directed for taking fresh steps on present
address, and address of their posting. Steps were taken
by revisionist. Thereafter fresh report was submitted by
Registry of this Court on 23.08.2018, to the effect that
report of service on respondent no.2(i) and 2(ii) has not
been received, where respondent no.2(iii) was reported
to be served personally and was represented by his
counsel.
 Thereafter yet another report was given that
respondent no.2(i) could not be served as transferred
from Suratgarh to Jammu Cantt. and respondent no.2(ii)
could not be served as he was transferred from Jodhpur,
as Garrison Engineer, Silchar, Asram. Thereafter
revisionist was directed to serve respondent no.2(i) and
respondent no.2(ii) on the address as per their
employees code. There was yet another report dated
14.11.2019, that respondent no.2(i) and 2(ii) has been
received with report, that not received as it was
received after the date fixed in the notices. Hence in
view of the said it would they have acquired knowledge
of pendency of Criminal Revision and had voided to
receive notice to avoid their participation.
 Even otherwise also it is the action of rejection of

the complaint by the trial court, it is court's action,
which is under challenge. The effective need of
participation for contesting case would arise, only when
the complaint is accepted to heard, which is the stage,
which has yet to be heard on merits. Thus, the revision
is being heard finally after hearing the counsel for the
respondent no.2(iii) and the Government Advocate.
 The revisionist herein has filed a complaint, which
was registered as Criminal Complaint No.3756 of 2017,
Manish Chandra Joshi vs. Kamal Deep Sharma and
other before the court of Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haldwani District Nainital in the complaint
thus filed by the revisionist on 10.08.2017 he has
contended that his late father, who was working with
M.E.S. Department as Electrical Engineer at the time
when he was working as an Electrician on an electric
pole on 14.06.2013, prior to his start of work the main
switch was put off by him, but later on, on account of
mistake of the then Assistant Garrison Engineer and
other Engineers, who are responsible, somehow the
main switch was put "on" and the electricity flowed in
the pole on which he was working and later on he
received electric shock, while working on pole during
duty hours, he succumbed to the injuries and died. Post
mortem was conducted on him on the same day.
 For getting an appropriate trial conducted in
relation to the set of allegations, which he has leveled
against officers concerned in the department on account
of their derelictions in discharging of duties for putting
switch on. He filed a complaint on 10.08.2017 and the
said complaint has been rejected by the impugned order
dated 09.02.2018 alleging thereof that the set of
allegations could not be established and hence in view
of the provisions contained under Section 203 IPC, the
complaint has been rejected holding that it cannot be
entertained.
 After having considered the finding, which has
been recorded by the Court of Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haldwani in the impugned order dated
09.02.2018 and also the statement as it has been
recorded under 202 Cr.P.C., this Court is of the view
that the correct appreciation to statements made under
Section 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C. was not complied with

by the court concerned and its appreciation has not been
made in the appropriate manner. This Court considered
the statement made under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and other
material on record, including the proceedings as held
under Section 202 Cr.P.C., this Court is of the view that
it prima facie establishes the negligence on part of the
respondents against whom the complaint was
registered. Since it was a complaint case and it was an
action which revisionist wanted to determine the actual
liability in relation to the person responsive and
working in the department who was responsible for the
incident resulting into death of the father. This Court is
of the view that the reason assigned in the impugned
order dated 09.02.2018 rejecting his complaint cannot
be sustained. The reason to reject the complaint, was
because the complaint referred that someone switch on
the main switch, since the word "someone" was used
there was no specific allegation made against any
specific person, that could not be because complainant
was not present when the main switch was switched on,
hence obviously could not have named a person, it was
to be only determined after trial only on registering the
complaint. Hence, the revision is allowed and the
impugned order dated 09.02.2018 is quashed. The
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haldwani,
District Nainital is directed to register the complaint
case and proceed in accordance with law.
